# Astralis

> An interactive cosmic atlas for researchers, students and the curious — explore planets, moons, stars, galaxies, black holes, nebulae and meteors with NASA-grade imagery, deep-dive data, mission tracking, comparisons and an AI research assistant that cites peer-reviewed sources.

Astralis is a free, browser-based reference for astronomy. It catalogues celestial bodies, tracks current and upcoming space missions worldwide, lets users compare bodies side-by-side, and includes a community forum and AI research assistant that links out to arXiv, NASA ADS and journal publications.

## Pages

- [Home](/): Browse and search the full atlas of celestial bodies and featured missions.
- [Compare](/compare): Place any two celestial bodies side by side and compare their vital statistics.
- [Missions](/missions): Live and upcoming space missions, organised by country and status.
- [Research](/research): AI research assistant for astronomy questions with peer-reviewed citations.
- [Forum](/forum): Community discussions on astronomy, missions and research papers.

## Categories

- [Planets](/category/planets): Worlds orbiting our Sun.
- [Moons](/category/moons): Natural satellites of strange beauty.
- [Stars](/category/stars): From red dwarfs to hypergiants.
- [Galaxies](/category/galaxies): Island universes of stars.
- [Black Holes](/category/black-holes): Gravity beyond escape.
- [Nebulae](/category/nebulae): Stellar nurseries and graveyards.
- [Meteors](/category/meteors): Wanderers and impactors.
